citacoes.trecho: Code generation refers to the automatic creation of source code from natural language descriptions (e.g. prompts with problem descriptions and test cases) [1].
We then submit a prompt to Ollama using the specified model, following this prompt format:
To assist LLMs in identifying and correcting logic errors, we propose a Hint-Driven Prompting methodology, which encompasses two approaches: USACO Hint Prompting and GPT-4o Refined Hint Prompting.
By providing LLMs with the official USACO solution hints in English, it simplifies one of the steps of the problem solving process.
Specifically, the USACO solution hints written in English is first provided to GPT-4o along with the original problem statement for context.
The refined solution hints generated by GPT-4o are subsequently fed into the LLMs, and their generated code are evaluated in the same manner as before.
Note that this methodology is only meant to simulate a human giving a LLM clear, step by step instructions.
In this section, we propose a Syntax Mitigation Prompt that can effectively reduce primary syntax bugs across various models.
Additionally, we add in simple Python error examples and variations to ensure that the model doesn't make those errors again.
Note: This Syntax Mitigation Prompt is given alongside the GPT-4o refined hints for LLMs to generate code.
Five models out of 11 models tested were selected to show an overall decrease in syntax bugs, including Deepseek-Coder 33B, Codellama 70B, Codegemma 7B, Llama 3 8B, and GPT-4o.
Across all 11 LLMs we evaluate, the overall error distribution shows 36.8% logical failures, meaning that the majority of errors stem from code that runs but produces incorrect outcomes.
Specifically, 36.8% of the test cases that fail are due to logic errors in the code generated by LLMs.
Moreover, once an LLM generates an incorrect solution, subsequent iterations relying on that code may propagate these errors, leading to more complex problems that are harder to identify and resolve.
This is evident from the high occurrence of “timeout” errors when evaluating code on our proposed USACO benchmark, which features complex test cases.
They also suffer from “data contamination” [19] [20] [21] when problems overlap with LLM training datasets [22], which skews reported performance [23] [24] [25].
First, USACO is less likely to be included in training data compared to other coding platforms like CodeForces, minimizing concerns of benchmark leakage and overfitting [21].
Furthermore, several works have revealed the security issues of LLM generated code and the introduction of vulnerabilities through the use of LLMs [48] [49] [50].

In the case of Codestral 22B, there is only a marginal improvement with the USACO hints, with test cases passed slightly increasing from 423 to 424, but a drop to 73 test cases following the GPT-4o refined hints which can be explained by a large surge in IndentationError.
The findings of our study may be limited by the relatively small size of the USACO dataset.

qualidade.justificativa: Três questões de pesquisa explícitas (benchmark, tipos de erro, abordagens sem retreinamento) e contribuições listadas.

Descreve a coleta, o prompt base, a geração via Ollama, a verificação com limite de 5 s e a pontuação.
